skill.name: context-compression
skill.description: Guide agents to compress long coding sessions into structured summaries that preserve files, decisions, state, and next steps.
skill.summary: Structured context compression for long-running agent sessions and large codebase work.

content.value_statement: Long agent sessions lose important files, decisions, and next steps when context is compressed too aggressively. This skill provides structured compression and evaluation methods that preserve usable context while reducing token usage.
actual_capabilities: Explains anchored iterative summarization, opaque compression, and regenerative summaries.
Recommends compression triggers based on context utilization and task boundaries.
Provides structured sections for session intent, files, decisions, state, and next steps.
Defines probe types and scoring dimensions for compression quality testing.
Includes a Python evaluator with heuristic scoring and summarizer utilities.
limitations: The evaluator uses stubbed judge calls and simplified token estimates.
It does not perform live compression automatically without agent implementation work.
Regex-based extraction may miss complex file operations or decisions.
Benchmark numbers are reference material, not a guarantee for every workflow.

use_cases.title: Preserve Long Debugging Context
use_cases.description: Keep errors, modified files, and remaining tests visible after context compaction.

use_cases.title: Design Agent Memory Summaries
use_cases.description: Build structured summary sections for agents that run across many turns.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Compression Quality
use_cases.description: Use probes and rubric dimensions to compare compression strategies.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Current Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this conversation into sections for intent, files, decisions, current state, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Compression Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this agent workflow, choose a compression trigger and summary structure. Explain the trade-offs for token usage and continuity.

prompt_templates.title: Build Evaluation Probes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create recall, artifact, continuation, and decision probes for this compressed session. Include expected answers and scoring focus.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Compression Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these summaries across compression cycles. Identify lost facts, missing files, changed decisions, and actions to improve retention.

output_examples.input: A long debugging conversation nearing context limits.
output_examples.output: A structured summary with session intent, root cause, files read, files modified, test status, and next steps.

output_examples.input: A compressed session and a set of probe questions.
output: Recall results highlight preserved technical facts.
Artifact results list missing file tracking details.
Continuation results show whether work can resume without re-reading context.

output_examples.input: A planned agent workflow for a large codebase migration.
output_examples.output: A three-phase plan that turns exploration into research notes, an implementation specification, and focused execution context.

best_practices: Compress at clear thresholds and keep the recent working window visible.
Use explicit sections for files, decisions, current state, and next steps.
Test summaries with probes before relying on them for long tasks.
anti_patterns: Optimizing only for the smallest summary without measuring re-fetching cost.
Regenerating full summaries repeatedly without checking information drift.
Treating file tracking as a normal prose summary problem.

faq.question: Does this skill run compression automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategies, templates, and evaluation utilities that an agent or developer can implement.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that need long-session context management.

faq.question: What compression method does it recommend?
faq.answer: It generally favors anchored iterative summarization when file tracking and decision retention matter.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Python evaluator, but the LLM judge call is a stub for demonstration.

faq.question: How should I measure quality?
faq.answer: Use recall, artifact, continuation, and decision probes against compressed context.

faq.question: Will it reduce all token costs?
faq.answer: No. It aims to reduce total tokens per task, not only tokens per request.
